title: Building efficient hybrid context query for LLM grounding: Simrat Hanspal
talk_summary: A Hasura evangelist demos building a hybrid RAG product-search pipeline where an LLM generates GraphQL queries against a unified API over relational + vector data, covering semantic, structured, and hybrid queries. The one substantive engineering lesson is that LLM-generated queries must be executed under a restricted DB role, since an unrestricted demo let a prompt-injected 'insert' mutation actually write to the database.

takeaways.technique: Least-privilege execution role for LLM-generated queries
takeaways.what_they_do: The LLM emits a GraphQL query/mutation that is executed directly against the data API; they define a dedicated role with only select permission so generated mutations fail at the DB layer rather than relying on prompt instructions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we are going to be defining a new role with very restricted permissions so that we only provide select permission

takeaways.technique: Adversarial 'evil intent' test case in the demo suite
takeaways.what_they_do: Alongside happy-path semantic/structured/hybrid queries they explicitly run a malicious insert query to prove the guardrail blocks it, then re-run the same attack after adding the role.
takeaways.evidence_quote: let's say I had an evil intent and I wanted to execute a malicious query

takeaways.technique: Single LLM-generated query spanning semantic + structured filters
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of separate retrieval paths, the model decomposes a natural-language request into one query combining a vector-similarity clause and structured field filters (price range, category), executed against one unified API.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it identified amazing essential oil diffuser as the semantic search query and then the price filter which is between 500,000

takeaways.technique: Auto-vectorize on write via DB event trigger
takeaways.what_they_do: A database event hook vectorizes new records into the vector store at insert time, so the retrieval index is always current without a separate sync job.
takeaways.evidence_quote: as in when a new record got inserted into my for CR table it got autov vectorized and saved in my Vector DB
